# Shroom Labs

> Shroom Labs keeps Shrooly mushroom chambers growing after the Shrooly app stopped working. It offers free OpenShrooly firmware that installs from a browser, free culinary grow profiles, paid Chef's line profiles, and Grow Coach with Autopilot.

Shrooly is a smart mushroom fruiting chamber. Since August 2025 many owners report the Shrooly app will not sign in, support does not answer, and orders did not arrive. The chamber itself still works.

OpenShrooly is free, open source software that replaces the stock Shrooly software, so the chamber runs on your own Wi-Fi with no Shrooly app. It was started by Graham Stewart (grahamsz). Shroom Labs builds on his work, signs each release, and offers a browser installer: Chrome or Edge on a computer, a USB-C data cable, about 5 minutes. Updates then install over Wi-Fi. An account is optional; it adds a phone dashboard and email alerts.

Shroom Labs also publishes researched grow profiles for culinary and functional mushrooms, with temperature, humidity, fresh air, and light for every stage. The basic profiles are free. The Chef's line adds paid specialty methods for a better harvest, $2.99 to $3.99 each, as one-time purchases.

Grow Coach reads a linked chamber's live readings and recommends humidity and temperature changes for the culinary profile being grown. Autopilot can make those changes itself, inside the profile's safe range, and logs every decision with the reason. Grow Coach is $4.99 a month or $49 a year.

Shroom Labs is not made by or affiliated with the company behind Shrooly.

All grow numbers on this site come from the published grow profiles. Temperatures are in °C with °F in brackets.

## Bring a Shrooly back

- [Install on your Shrooly](https://shroomlabs.io/install): put free OpenShrooly firmware on a Shrooly from Chrome or Edge with a USB-C data cable in about 5 minutes. Signed releases only.
- [What happened to Shrooly?](https://shroomlabs.io/what-happened-to-shrooly): We could not find a public shutdown notice from the company that made Shrooly. Its last customer update was July 31, 2025. Since August 2025 many owners report the app will not sign in, support does not answer, and orders did not arrive. Your chamber can still run on free community software.
- [Reuse your Shrooly](https://shroomlabs.io/reuse-your-shrooly): Yes, you can reuse your Shrooly. Free, open source software called OpenShrooly replaces the stock software, so the chamber runs on your own Wi-Fi with no Shrooly app. You install it from Chrome or Edge with a USB-C cable in about 5 minutes. Shroom Labs adds grow profiles and an optional phone dashboard.
- [Shrooly FAQ](https://shroomlabs.io/shrooly-faq): Short version: many Shrooly owners lost the app in 2025, and the company has not said why. The chamber itself still works. Free OpenShrooly firmware runs it on your own Wi-Fi with no Shrooly app, and you can install it from Chrome or Edge in about 5 minutes. Answers to the questions owners ask most are below.
- [Shrooly pods: how to refill or replace one](https://shroomlabs.io/shrooly-pods): Owners report that new Shrooly pods are hard or impossible to get. You have three ways forward: get a second flush from the pod you have, refill a pod with your own substrate if you can work clean, or, easiest of all, replace it with a ready to fruit grow block or all in one bag that fits the chamber. With free OpenShrooly software, the chamber runs any block, no pod needed.
- [Shrooly shut down? Your options](https://shroomlabs.io/shrooly-alternatives): We could not find a public shutdown notice, but many owners report the Shrooly app no longer signs in and pods are hard to get. You still have four good options: revive the chamber with free software, run it by hand, build a simple chamber of your own, or grow in a plastic tub. The first keeps the hardware you paid for working.
- [Join the Shroom Labs beta](https://shroomlabs.io/beta): If your Shrooly sits unused because the app stopped working, this beta puts it back to work. It is free. Spots are limited to the first 50 linked chambers.
- [Link a chamber](https://shroomlabs.io/claim): link a chamber to your account to see it on your phone and get grow alerts by email. Optional. It works fully on your Wi-Fi without it.

## Grow Coach and Autopilot

- [Grow Coach](https://shroomlabs.io/coach): reads your chamber's live readings and recommends humidity and temperature changes for the culinary profile you are growing. Autopilot makes those changes for you inside the profile's safe range. $4.99 a month or $49 a year. Cancel anytime.

## Grow guides

- [Mushroom growing conditions for every species](https://shroomlabs.io/grow): one table with fruiting temperature, humidity, light, and days for each species.
- [Chef's line](https://shroomlabs.io/chefs-line): paid specialty grow profiles for a better harvest. Each is a one-time purchase.
- [How to grow mushrooms at home](https://shroomlabs.io/guides/grow-mushrooms-at-home): The easiest way to grow mushrooms at home is to start with an oyster or lion's mane kit or a colonized block, keep it at 85 to 95% humidity with regular fresh air, give it indirect light, and keep the room cool. Most kits start forming mushrooms one to two weeks after you open them. When that works, a fruiting chamber makes every grow repeatable.
- [What is the easiest mushroom to grow at home?](https://shroomlabs.io/guides/easiest-mushrooms-to-grow): Oyster mushrooms are the easiest mushroom to grow at home. Pearl and blue oyster colonize fast, shrug off small mistakes, and run about 29 and 25 days in their profiles from the start of colonization to the end of the first harvest window. Lion's mane is a close second and just as good in a kit.
- [Grow kit vs monotub vs smart chamber](https://shroomlabs.io/guides/grow-kit-vs-monotub-vs-smart-chamber): A grow kit is the cheapest and simplest way to get a first harvest. A monotub gives bigger harvests from bulk substrate but takes more hands on work and clean technique. A smart fruiting chamber holds humidity, fresh air, and light for you, and some also manage temperature, so results repeat, but it costs more up front.
- [How much humidity and fresh air do mushrooms need?](https://shroomlabs.io/guides/humidity-and-fresh-air): Most culinary mushrooms need 86 to 95% humidity while pins form and 82 to 93% while they fruit, plus regular fresh air to clear the carbon dioxide they breathe out. Too little humidity gives dry, cracked caps and stalled pins. Too little fresh air gives long stems and small caps. The two pull against each other, so the goal is steady humidity with gentle, regular air changes.
- [Why are my mushrooms not pinning?](https://shroomlabs.io/guides/mushrooms-not-pinning): Mushrooms usually fail to pin for one of two reasons: the block is not fully colonized yet, or nothing has told it to fruit. Pins form when the block is fully white and then gets a change: cooler air, more fresh air, higher humidity, and light. Check those four, give it a week, and most blocks start to pin.
- [Why do my mushrooms have long stems and small caps?](https://shroomlabs.io/guides/leggy-mushroom-stems): Long, thin stems with small caps almost always mean too much carbon dioxide. The mushrooms are stretching to reach fresh air. Add more air changes, open more holes, or fan more often. If air is good, check light next: mushrooms in a dark corner also stretch toward the nearest light.
- [Why are my mushroom caps dry or cracked?](https://shroomlabs.io/guides/dry-cracked-mushroom-caps): Dry, cracked, or curled caps mean the mushrooms are losing water faster than the block can supply it. Usually the air is drier than the species wants, or a fan, heater, or vent is blowing straight on them. Raise humidity, block direct airflow, and keep air changes gentle. Most culinary profiles here fruit at 82 to 93% humidity.
- [Is my mushroom block contaminated?](https://shroomlabs.io/guides/mushroom-contamination): Healthy mycelium is white, sometimes with yellow or amber drops. Contamination usually shows as color: green, blue-green, black, pink, or orange patches, or wet, slimy spots that smell sour. If you see colored mold, bag the block, take it outside without opening it, and clean the area. Do not eat mushrooms from a moldy block.
- [Mushroom growing terms, explained plainly](https://shroomlabs.io/guides/mushroom-growing-glossary): Mushroom growing has its own words, but the ideas are simple. Mycelium is the living network that eats the food you give it. Spawn is mycelium grown on grain, used to seed a bigger batch of substrate, which is the food. Colonization is the mycelium filling that food. Pinning is when tiny mushrooms appear. A flush is one wave of mushrooms. Below are the terms you will meet most, grouped by when you meet them.
- [Shrooly app not working? What you can do](https://shroomlabs.io/guides/shrooly-app-not-working): Since about August 2025, many owners report that the Shrooly app will not log in or start a grow, often with a no internet connection error, and that support does not reply. If that is what you see, the problem is likely on the app's servers, not your phone. You can still use the chamber: free, open source OpenShrooly firmware runs it over your own Wi-Fi from a web page, with no app or cloud account.
- [How long does it take to grow mushrooms?](https://shroomlabs.io/guides/how-long-to-grow-mushrooms): Most culinary mushrooms take 20 to 78 days at home, from the start of colonization to the end of the first harvest. Oysters are fastest: pink oyster takes about 20 days and pearl oyster about 29. Shiitake and reishi take 74 to 77 days. From a fully colonized kit, most species fruit in one to three weeks.
- [Mushroom grow kit not growing? Check these causes](https://shroomlabs.io/guides/mushroom-grow-kit-not-growing): Most grow kits that do nothing have one of five problems: the block is not fully colonized, the room is too warm or too cold, the air is too dry, there is too little fresh air, or the kit was not opened where it needs to be. Work through the checklist below in order. A healthy kit usually pins within one to two weeks once all five are right.

## Free grow tools

- [Mushroom grow timeline calculator](https://shroomlabs.io/tools/grow-timeline): Pick a mushroom and the day you start, and this calculator lists the date each stage begins, the temperature, humidity, fresh air, and light to use, and your first harvest window. Totals run from 20 days for pink oyster to 78 days for turkey tail. You can save every stage to your calendar as an .ics file.
- [Mushroom fresh air and humidity planner](https://shroomlabs.io/tools/fresh-air-planner): Enter your chamber size and fan flow, and this planner works out how many times an hour your fan replaces the air in the chamber, next to the humidity and fan cycle your mushroom's profile uses. Oyster growing rooms are commonly run at about 4 to 6 fresh air changes an hour while fruiting, so you get a number to compare against.

## Grow profiles by species

- [How to grow Beech / Buna Shimeji](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/beech-shimeji): Beech / Buna Shimeji (Hypsizygus tessulatus), also called brown beech mushroom or buna shimeji, takes about 40 days to grow at home, from spawn to the end of the first harvest. Colonize at 22 °C (72 °F) in the dark, then fruit at 15 °C (59 °F) and 90% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h of light a day.
- [How to grow Beech Shimeji: tight bouquet](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/beech-shimeji-bouquet): Paid culinary Profile, $2.99. About 40 days from start to fruit.
- [How to grow Blue Oyster](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/blue-oyster): Blue Oyster (Pleurotus ostreatus var. columbinus), also called Pleurotus columbinus, takes about 25 days to grow at home, from spawn to the end of the first harvest. Colonize at 22 °C (72 °F) in the dark, then fruit at 14 °C (57 °F) and 87% humidity with plenty of fresh air and 12 h of light a day.
- [How to grow Button / Cremini](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/button-cremini): Button / Cremini (Agaricus bisporus), also called white button or cremini, takes about 36 days to grow at home, from spawn to the end of the first harvest. Colonize at 24 °C (75 °F) in the dark, then fruit at 16 °C (61 °F) and 88% humidity with moderate fresh air and no light.
- [How to grow Chestnut Mushroom](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/chestnut): Chestnut Mushroom (Pholiota adiposa), also called fat Pholiota, takes about 34 days to grow at home, from spawn to the end of the first harvest. Colonize at 23 °C (73 °F) in the dark, then fruit at 15 °C (59 °F) and 92% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h of light a day.
- [How to grow Chestnut: long stem](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/chestnut-long-stem): Paid culinary Profile, $2.99. About 34 days from start to fruit.
- [How to grow Cordyceps militaris](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/cordyceps-militaris): Cordyceps militaris, also called scarlet caterpillar club, takes about 57 days to grow at home, from spawn to the end of the first harvest. Colonize at 20 °C (68 °F) in the dark, then fruit at 18 °C (64 °F) and 84% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h of light a day.
- [How to grow Cordyceps: deep orange under pink light](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/cordyceps-high-color): Paid culinary Profile, $3.99. About 57 days from start to fruit.
- [How to grow Elm Oyster](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/elm-oyster): Elm Oyster (Hypsizygus ulmarius), also called elm leech, takes about 31 days to grow at home, from spawn to the end of the first harvest. Colonize at 22 °C (72 °F) in the dark, then fruit at 15 °C (59 °F) and 86% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h of light a day.
- [How to grow Enoki](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/enoki): Enoki (Flammulina velutipes), also called enokitake or golden needle mushroom, takes about 43 days to grow at home, from spawn to the end of the first harvest. Colonize at 22 °C (72 °F) in the dark, then fruit at 15 °C (59 °F) and 93% humidity with little fresh air and no light.
- [How to grow Golden Oyster](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/golden-oyster): Golden Oyster (Pleurotus citrinopileatus), also called yellow oyster or tamogitake, takes about 24 days to grow at home, from spawn to the end of the first harvest. Colonize at 25 °C (77 °F) in the dark, then fruit at 21 °C (70 °F) and 87% humidity with plenty of fresh air and 12 h of light a day.
- [How to grow Golden Oyster: deep yellow](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/golden-oyster-deep-yellow): Paid culinary Profile, $2.99. About 24 days from start to fruit.
- [How to grow King Oyster](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/king-oyster): King Oyster (Pleurotus eryngii), also called king trumpet or French horn mushroom, takes about 38 days to grow at home, from spawn to the end of the first harvest. Colonize at 22 °C (72 °F) in the dark, then fruit at 15 °C (59 °F) and 82% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h of light a day.
- [How to grow King Oyster: thick-stem method](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/king-oyster-thick-stem): Paid culinary Profile, $2.99. About 43 days from start to fruit.
- [How to grow Lion's Mane](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/lions-mane): Lion's Mane (Hericium erinaceus), also called bearded tooth or pom pom mushroom, takes about 33 days to grow at home, from spawn to the end of the first harvest. Colonize at 22 °C (72 °F) in the dark, then fruit at 17 °C (63 °F) and 90% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h of light a day.
- [How to grow Lion's Mane: dense white heads](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/lions-mane-dense-head): Paid culinary Profile, $3.99. About 32 days from start to fruit.
- [How to grow Maitake](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/maitake): Maitake (Grifola frondosa), also called hen of the woods or sheep's head, takes about 54 days to grow at home, from spawn to the end of the first harvest. Colonize at 22 °C (72 °F) in the dark, then fruit at 16 °C (61 °F) and 88% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h of light a day.
- [How to grow Nameko](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/nameko): Nameko (Pholiota microspora), also called butterscotch mushroom, takes about 39 days to grow at home, from spawn to the end of the first harvest. Colonize at 22 °C (72 °F) in the dark, then fruit at 14 °C (57 °F) and 93% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h of light a day.
- [How to grow Pearl Oyster](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/pearl-oyster): Pearl Oyster (Pleurotus ostreatus), also called oyster mushroom or hiratake, takes about 29 days to grow at home, from spawn to the end of the first harvest. Colonize at 24 °C (75 °F) in the dark, then fruit at 16 °C (61 °F) and 88% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h of light a day.

Colonize at 27 °C (81 °F) in the dark, then fruit at 24 °C (75 °F) and 86% humidity with plenty of fresh air and 12 h of light a day.

- [How to grow Pioppino](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/pioppino): Pioppino (Cyclocybe aegerita), also called black poplar mushroom or Agrocybe aegerita, takes about 31 days to grow at home, from spawn to the end of the first harvest. Colonize at 25 °C (77 °F) in the dark, then fruit at 16 °C (61 °F) and 86% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h of light a day.
- [How to grow Reishi](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/reishi): Reishi (Ganoderma lucidum), also called lingzhi or varnished conk, takes about 77 days to grow at home, from spawn to the end of the first harvest. Colonize at 27 °C (81 °F) in the dark, then fruit at 23 °C (73 °F) and 85% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h of light a day.
- [How to grow Shiitake](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/shiitake): Shiitake (Lentinula edodes), also called black forest mushroom or xiang gu, takes about 74 days to grow at home, from spawn to the end of the first harvest. ## Off-menu research profiles

Psilocybin mushrooms are illegal to grow, possess, or sell in most countries and under US federal law. This information is published for educational, research and harm-reduction purposes only. Check the laws where you live. Shroom Labs does not sell spores, cultures or psilocybin products. Spore laws vary by state and country, and some US states ban spores outright. Where they are sold, spores are sold for microscopy only.

- [Acadian Coast (Psilocybe cubensis)](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/acadian-coast): fruits at 22 °C (72 °F) and 90% humidity, about 32 days from start to fruit.
- [B+ (Psilocybe cubensis)](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/b-plus): fruits at 21 °C (70 °F) and 89% humidity, about 32 days from start to fruit.
- [Golden Teacher (Psilocybe cubensis)](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/golden-teacher): fruits at 22 °C (72 °F) and 90% humidity, about 32 days from start to fruit.
- [Penis Envy (Psilocybe cubensis)](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/penis-envy): fruits at 22 °C (72 °F) and 90% humidity, about 50 days from start to fruit.
- [Psilocybe cyanescens](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/p-cyanescens): fruits at 15 °C (59 °F) and 90% humidity, about 52 days from start to fruit.
- [Psilocybe natalensis](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/p-natalensis): fruits at 23 °C (73 °F) and 90% humidity, about 29 days from start to fruit.
- [Treasure Coast (Psilocybe cubensis)](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/treasure-coast): fruits at 22 °C (72 °F) and 90% humidity, about 32 days from start to fruit.
